text:
The most likely corrupted element is **M5**, the OTA tail current source. It is the only device whose operating point is clearly broken: it sits in triode (Vds = 0.282 V vs. Vdsat = 0.562 V) and carries 5.74 µA against the 10 µA its mirror M6 should deliver. Its W = 0.42 µm is also smaller than M6's 0.49 µm, so the mirror ratio is off. A starved tail reduces the input-pair gm and the OTA's bandwidth, which would pull f0 low, consistent with 14.96 Hz vs. a 25.2–30.8 Hz target.

M3 is the second candidate because it has the largest f0 sensitivity (+88%). Its pair partner M4 matches it in size, though, so M3 looks nominal, and its high sensitivity is more likely a consequence of the OTA's dynamics than a fault. Rd2 is third because it sets the input common mode (vm ≈ 0.9 V), and that bias leaves too little headroom for the tail to saturate. This is my reading of the operating-point tables and sensitivities, not a simulation, so the ranking is a best estimate.

Its tail current is about 5.7 uA instead of about 10 uA, and at vm = 0.9 V it is pushed into triode, which starves the input pair, lowers OTA gm/GBW and pulls f0 down to about 15 Hz."}
